messages:
anya_support: Customer report: EU customers seeing p95=12-18s, intermittent 502/503, and an unexpected spike in token usage/billing. They attach response headers showing x-redwood-region: ap-southeast-1 while they explicitly set X-Region: eu-west-1. Can someone look?

devon_infra: Do we have a request id or sample request?

anya_support: They sent this curl and a response dump:
```\ncurl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/generate \\ 
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-ORG-abc123\" \\ 
  -H \"X-Region: eu-west-1\" \\ 
  -d '{"model":"rw1-medium","input":"hello"}'
```
Response headers they saw: `x-redwood-region: ap-southeast-1`, `x-request-id: r-abc12345`, `x-redwood-queue-time: 16.2s`.

ops-bot: autoscaler: eu-west reserved pool utilization 100% (gpus 24/24), queue depth=512, spillover_active=true

miriam_sre: If queue depth that high and spillover=true we'll route per fallback policy. Need to check whether cancellation was sent when fallback executed.

devon_infra: Traced r-abc12345: eval at eu-west -> OVER_CAPACITY -> fallback to ap-southeast; us-east not involved. But eu-west queue kept the job for ~18s and we dispatched a duplicate to ap-southeast. Cancellation propagation between regions failed for that request id.

liu_prodops: That would explain the billing bump (duplicate execution) and the long p95 (queue + fallback exec). Any auth anomalies?

anya_support: Customer logs also show intermittent 403: \"token scope restricted to eu-west\" for some retries on fallback region. They use org-scoped tokens that are region-bound.

sam_billing: If duplicate execs are confirmed we need to flag for credit. Please include list of request ids.

miriam_sre: Quick mitigation options: 1) Pin this org to eu-west for short window, 2) disable auto-fallback for routes where token scope != global, 3) drain eu-west queue and cancel duplicates.

devon_infra: Agreed. Root cause appears to be twofold: a) cancellation propagation across regions relies on async pub/sub and had a message loss window when queues spike, b) routing logic doesn't validate token scope before choosing a fallback region. Also sticky-window logic intended to avoid duplicates had default timeout that doesn't cover queued jobs.

liu_prodops: I'm going to apply an org-level pin to keep customer traffic in eu-west for 4 hours. Notifying customer now.

ops-bot: config: pin(org=org-5678, region=eu-west-1, expires=2026-03-12T19:00:00Z) -> applied

devon_infra: I'm rolling a canary patch to the cancel-propagation path that makes cross-region cancels synchronous for the same request-id (10% canary in eu-west). Kicking off now.

ops-bot: deploy: cancel-prop-fix v2026.03.12-canary -> started (canary=10% eu-west)

miriam_sre: For auth: short-term we should stop sending fallback when token scope header says regional. Long-term: implement control-plane token-exchange so fallback can exchange or re-scope tokens safely if customer allows.

anya_support: Repro steps I used to validate: 1) flood eu-west with 400 simultaneous requests using X-Region=eu-west-1, 2) watch reserved pool saturation and autoscaler delay, 3) confirm fallback to ap-southeast, 4) observe eu-west queue retention 12-22s and duplicate execution in fallback region, 5) see 403s on fallback when token scoped. Script saved to s3.

devon_infra: Logs (sanitized):
```\n[eu-west] 2026-03-12T10:05:02Z route_eval: OVER_CAPACITY threshold=0.95
[eu-west] 2026-03-12T10:05:02Z enqueue: qpos=498
[eu-west] 2026-03-12T10:05:20Z cancel: propagated=false
[ap-southeast] 2026-03-12T10:05:03Z receive: routed_from=eu-west request_id=r-abc12345
[ap-southeast] 2026-03-12T10:05:04Z exec_start request_id=r-abc12345
[ap-southeast] 2026-03-12T10:05:05Z auth: token_scope=eu-west-only -> 403
```

sam_billing: Please drop a CSV of affected request ids and timestamps. We’ll prepare customer credits if duplicates are confirmed.

liu_prodops: Added items to incident board: P0 cancel-propagation patch (devon), P0 token-scope pre-check in router (miriam), P1 metric: duplicate-exec billing delta by request-id (sam), P2 reduce queued retention before failover and tighten sticky-window (devon).

devon_infra: Canary looks healthy for 10% (no duplicates observed in canary window). Rolling to 50% for eu-west now.

ops-bot: deploy: cancel-prop-fix -> progressing (canary=50% eu-west)

miriam_sre: I'm drafting the router change: short-circuit fallback for regional tokens and add an opt-in control-plane token exchange flow. Will PR today.

anya_support: Notified customer about pin and that we're investigating billing credits. They asked for ETA — given canary moving to 50% I told them we expect a fix/rollback within 3 hours.

devon_infra: Also fixed sticky-window default from 30s -> 8s for queued jobs; follow-up config PR pending. That reduces duplicate risk during transient queue spikes.

sam_billing: Got the request-id list; prepped draft credit for affected invoices.

anya_support: Saving repros: s3://redwood-support/repros/eu-spillover-20260312.sh and will attach to ticket.

liu_prodops: Please add postmortem once router & auth fixes are merged. Also log customer-facing note for billing ops.

miriam_sre: Will open the postmortem doc and link owners.

anya_support: Closing this thread for now — will reopen if canary regresses. Thanks all :wave:
